subject: FinServCo: request for incident response capability details and notification procedures
messages:
From: Alice Martin <alice.martin@finserv.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: secops@finserv.com
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 16:14:00 -0400
Subject: Request: IR capability and notification procedures

Hi Jordan,

Quick intro — I’m Alice Martin (Security Operations, FinServCo). We’re running a vendor assessment ahead of a procurement milestone and need a few items from Redwood to complete our compliance review. Could you share the following by EOD next Wednesday (July 29)?

1) The latest incident response plan (IRP) or a customer-facing summary of notification procedures.
2) Your escalation/contact matrix for security incidents (who we call for S1/S2, after-hours contact).
3) SIG/CAIQ mapping or a short evidence list showing where notification SLAs and forensic procedures are documented.
4) Any current SLAs or commitments around customer notification timing (e.g., initial notification within X hours for confirmed data exposure).

If there are limitations on what you can share publicly, a redacted IRP + an internal-only drive link or a list of artifacts is fine. Also flag any step that would require a risk/contract conversation (e.g., forensic access, live tenant data requests).

Thanks — we’re trying to close procurement the week after next so timely responses help.

Best,
Alice Martin
Security Operations
FinServCo

Attachments: none

Ben — can you confirm you have the latest IRP PDF and SIG mapping assets? Evelyn — I’ll draft an initial customer note and share for edits.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Martin <alice.martin@finserv.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, secops@finserv.com
Date: Sat, 24 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinServCo: request for incident response capability details and notification procedures

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Attached is a customer-ready package and a short summary of our notification commitments. If anything needs more depth, Ben and I can follow up with a short screen share.

Summary (high level):
- Initial notification: For confirmed incidents impacting customer data categorized as Confidentiality/Integrity loss, we issue an initial notification within 4 hours of confirmation for Severity 1 events; for events under investigation we provide an interim update within 24 hours.
- Escalation contacts: We supply a role-based escalation matrix (Security Lead, Account Security Manager, CTO escalation). Direct on-call contact is provided to customers under enterprise contracts; role-based contact is provided for standard hosted accounts.
- Forensics & evidence: We provide event timelines, OCI/objstore logs, and redacted forensic artifacts. Live tenant forensic access requires a signed data access agreement; otherwise we provide exported logs and sanitized evidence.
- SIG/CAIQ: Attached is a mapping workbook that points to sections in our IRP, logging policy, and SOC artifacts that address notification and forensics.

Attachments (redacted):
- Redwood_IRP_v2.pdf (redacted customer-facing IRP)
- SIG_evidence_mapping.xlsx (SIG/CAIQ mapping + artifact references)
- Customer_Notification_Template.txt (short template for initial notification)

Links: https://drive.redwood.ai/secure/IRP_v2 (drive folder with permissions)
JIRA:SEC-478 (tracking FinServCo request)

If you want a signed SIG export or a completed CAIQ, that will need a brief SOW for signatures and takes ~5 business days to coordinate with our compliance team — we’ve included that as an option in the drive.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Security (acting)
Redwood Inference

--

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Martin <alice.martin@finserv.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, secops@finserv.com, Carl Reyes <carl.reyes@vendorsec.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2026 10:32:00 -0700
Subject: Notification: security incident affecting ingestion pipeline — initial impact and postmortem delivery

Alice / FinServCo secops — I’m notifying you of a security incident that affected the ingestion pipeline serving some hosted customer workloads. We’re sharing this quickly as a customer-facing notification plus an attached postmortem.

Timeline (brief):
- 2026-07-31 03:12 UTC — anomaly detected by runtime telemetry during a deploy window.
- 2026-07-31 03:25 UTC — engineering declared an incident and mitigations began.
- 2026-07-31 05:10 UTC — abnormal write to a transient buffer detected; no confirmed exfiltration to external systems.
- 2026-08-01 — deeper forensics run; no customer plaintext content observed in outbound flows; logs were preserved and are available.

Impact:
- A subset of ingestion jobs experienced delayed processing and transient metadata inconsistencies. We have no evidence of customer data exfiltration or unauthorized long-term access.

Remediations completed:
- Rolling code fix to the ingestion path deployed 2026-07-31 06:40 UTC.
- Two compensating config changes (rate limits and stricter input validation) reverted potential vectors.
- Additional monitoring and a dedicated runbook for deploy-time telemetry added.

Postmortem: Attached is the full incident postmortem (incident-psrm-20260802.pdf) that includes root cause analysis, timeline, artifact lists, and steps taken to prevent recurrence. A condensed customer executive summary is included at the top.

We will provide extracted logs and a sanitized artifact package on request (requires DSAR or data-access agreement depending on tenant). If FinServCo would like expanded evidence or a whiteboard session with the engineering team, we can schedule one — suggest JIRA:SEC-478 as the coordination thread.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Security (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident-psrm-20260802.pdf (pdf)
